Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/ExtendedBufferedReaderAgentTest.java` with 15 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering:

- Initial state (`getLastChar`/`getLineNumber`/`getPosition`/`getBytesRead` before any read)
- `close()` setting `lastChar` to EOF and blocking further reads
- Position tracking for single-char and bulk reads, including the EOF decrement quirk
- Zero-length reads not mutating state
- `mark()`/`reset()` restoring line number, position, last char, and bytes-read counters
- Byte tracking for ASCII and multi-byte (UTF-8 `é`) characters, and that it stays 0 without tracking enabled
- Boundary surrogate handling: a lone low surrogate throws `CharacterCodingException`, a trailing lone high surrogate does not throw and contributes 0 bytes
- `readLine()` with a lone trailing `\r` (no `\n`)
- `peek()` not altering externally observable state, and the subtler case where `peek()` after an explicit `mark()` overwrites the saved mark point (since `peek()` is implemented via the overridden `mark()`/`read()`/`reset()`)
- Line-number accounting for partial lines before a terminator is seen

Ran `./_tools/test.sh` for the full project — all 15 tests pass with no other `*AgentTest.java` files affected.
